subject.title: fix(browser): keep CDP cursor text previews UTF-16 safe

question: Does OpenClaw require page-side surrogate normalization for CDP cursor previews when JSON round-trips the value successfully and the existing Node stage already produces identical final output?
rationale: The code is mechanically coherent and well demonstrated, but accepting a second truncation owner depends on whether maintainers recognize a transport invariant or downstream failure not established by the submitted evidence.

options.title: Keep the existing pipeline
options.body: Decline the duplicate page helper unless a concrete CDP or downstream failure can be reproduced beyond the intermediate JavaScript string shape.

options.title: Require stronger failure proof
options.body: Keep the PR pending while requesting a reproducible CDP consumer error, corruption, or protocol-contract violation that the helper prevents.

options.title: Accept transport hardening
options.body: Sponsor page-side normalization as intentional defense-in-depth, then require a clean rebase and narrow invariant wording before merge.

recommendation.title: Keep the existing pipeline
recommendation.body: Decline the duplicate page helper unless a concrete CDP or downstream failure can be reproduced beyond the intermediate JavaScript string shape.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is recent work on browser CDP helpers and the same `cdp.ts` ownership boundary.
